subject: Hospitality
title: Keynote Speakers: The Draw
description: A micro-lesson that makes Keynote Speakers: The Draw usable.

hook.text: A-list keynote speakers command $50,000–250,000 per talk. The right name on the program can sell out a conference single-handedly.

buildup.text: Speaker bureaus manage talent and negotiate fees. The speaker market follows celebrity economics: scarcity, demand.

discovery.text: The best conference content isn't the keynote—it's the hallway conversations it sparks.

twist.text: Virtual keynotes during COVID revealed a truth: many $100,000 speakers delivered talks no better than free YouTube videos.

climax.text: Post-pandemic, conferences now invest more in interactive formats—workshops, roundtables, and peer exchanges.

punchline.text: $250,000 for 60 minutes on stage. But the real value walks the hallways after.

quiz.question: What did virtual keynotes during COVID reveal?
options: Many expensive speakers delivered talks no better than free YouTube content
